title: Abbreviations and Acronyms
source: Defence Forces Service Writing Manual 2024 (JP-04), Chapters 2 and 16
notes: The authorized abbreviation lists are at Annexes A-C to Chapter 16. The plugin can ship these lists as reference data.

rules.title: Full stops are not used within or after abbreviations
rules.description: Punctuation is not used within or after abbreviations, except when it is part of normal sentence punctuation.

autofix.description: Remove the full stops inside abbreviations.

rules.notes: Care needed with sentence-final full stops; the plugin should only flag full stops directly after 2+ capital letters mid-sentence.

rules.title: Full stops are not used between a person's initials
rules.description: Full stops are neither used between a person's initials nor between decorations.

rules.title: Unfamiliar abbreviations must be explained on first use
rules.description: Words abbreviated for convenience must be explained the first time they appear in the text, e.g. 'Joint Command and Staff College (JCSC)', and used consistently throughout.

rules.title: Abbreviation use must be consistent throughout
rules.description: There must be consistency of use throughout the document in headings, tables, and text.

rules.title: Abbreviations should not be introduced in a heading
rules.description: Abbreviations should not be introduced in a heading; where such words first appear in a heading, they should be written in full in that heading and the abbreviation introduced the first time the words appear in the text.

rules.title: Operational writing makes maximum use of authorized abbreviations
rules.description: Maximum use is to be made of abbreviations in operational writing except for the mandatory paragraph headings in operational and administrative orders; reported speech is always written in full.

rules.title: Only authorized abbreviations are used in operational writing
rules.description: In operational writing and signal messages only abbreviations listed in Chapter 16 are to be used, in addition to those specified in Paragraphs 267 and 268.

rules.title: Plurals of abbreviations follow the authorized rules
rules.description: Some abbreviations indicate both singular and plural and do not require an 's'; where 's' is added it goes at the end (e.g. C in Cs), and only for nouns, never verbs.

rules.title: Ampersand used in titles but not unit titles
rules.description: An ampersand (&) is to be used instead of 'and' where appropriate in titles (e.g. Ops & Trg), but it is not to be used in unit titles.
rules.notes: Ampersand is used in titles (e.g. Ops & Trg) but never in unit titles; distinguishing the two requires human review.

rules.title: Care needed with abbreviations read by allied forces or non-Service authorities
rules.description: Special care is needed to ensure that any abbreviation used in documents or messages to be read by members of allied forces or by non-Service authorities will be understood by them.

rules.title: Ranks and appointments are abbreviated in non-operational writing
rules.description: Ranks and appointments, designated regiments and corps, designated formations and units are abbreviated in non-operational writing.

rules.title: Formation/unit titles: number before description in Arabic numerals
rules.description: Titles of formations and units are normally written in abbreviated form with identifying numbers in Arabic numerals BEFORE the description: 32 Bde, 36 Sqn, LAB. The description must never precede the number.

rules.title: Quantitative numbers of formations/units are written in full
rules.description: Quantitative numbers of formations, units, ships and detachments are always written in full: 'Three brigades', not '3 bdes'.

rules.title: Dates in non-operational writing use the abbreviated day-month-year form
rules.description: Dates are abbreviated using the first 3 letters of the day of the week, the day of the month, the first 3 letters of the month and the last 2 figures of the year, e.g. 'Fri 1 Apr 13'. When dating a document, the day is omitted.
